items.title: Best & Worst Of 1997
items.author: deedub77
items.content:
Long time no see, but I’m finally back! Before we delve into 1998, I’ll be doing a little housekeeping, starting with a lot of 8Ball & MJG. In the meantime, I hope you enjoy the Best & Worst of 1997.

: (The X-Ecutioners – ): It just sounds dumber than the other nominees. (Frankie Cutlass – ), (Laylaw – , ), (DJ Muggs – ), (Lost Boyz – ), (The Beatnuts – ).

Worst Posse Record: “Painz & Stife”(Diamond D – Hatred, Passions And Infidelity): Diamond D serves up arguably the driest beat in his catalog for himself, Pete Rock, and (God bless the dead) Phife to rap over. Diamond’s verse is passable, but the beat, Pete, and Phife sound godawful. (Capone-N-Noreaga): Nore and his amateur band of cronies almost lulled me to sleep with their mundane street stanzas; and the whiny violin-led backdrop was annoying as shit. (Tha Alkaholiks – ): Tha Liks keep up their album tradition of making horrible posse records with The Lootpack, despite J-Ro doing all he can to break the pattern. (Busta Rhymes –): This uninspired Flipmode (Busta and Rampage)/Bad Boy (Puff and Mase) collab was memorable only for its mediocrity.

: (The Firm): The most generic, placeholder album title ever. : and (both by Domino).

: (Lil’ Raskull): No Limit Records was known for its cheesy, low-quality album cover artwork. Grapetree Records was a Southern-based Christian hip-hop label that copied NLR’s album-cover style, leaving a victim of the cheese. (Cross Movement): The members’ four floating heads inside a transparent God head floating through the clouds looks mad corny, and I find it hard to believe that God has a receding hairline. (LL Cool J): The grainy artwork is bad, but it becomes embarrassingly bad considering it was released on Def Jam during the label’s glory days. And what the hell is the picture of anyway? and (Domino): Virtually the same album gets two different but equally horrible album covers.

: … (Various Artists): Some of hip-hop’s biggest names of the era perform underwhelming karaoke. (Atmosphere): If vanilla was an album. (Murs): Easily the worst mixed album of the year. (Domino): was already mediocre, but Domino doubled down and released pretty much the same album with a slightly different title. A complete waste of wax, time, and energy.

: (Method Man on ): It’s only right that the king of aliases delivers the dopest alias of 1997. (Camp Lo – ), (Lil’ Raskull – ), (The Beatnuts – ).

Best Posse Record: “Beasts From The East” – (Lost Boyz): One word: Canibus. – (Frankie Cutlass): This gets a mention for Redman’s magnificent verse alone. – (Capone-N-Noreaga): A spirited response to Tha Dogg Pound’s “New York, New York. – (CRU): When verbal vitality carries the beat.

(The Notorious B.I.G.): The title was intended to be a play on the title of his debut, , but his untimely demise gave it new meaning. One Day It’ll All Make Sense (Common), (Tha Alkaholiks) (The X-Ecutioners) (EPMD)Silent Weapons For Quiet Wars (Killarmy).

: (Camp Lo)The homage to Ernie Barnes’ iconicpainting (made famous for its use on Marvin Gaye’salbum cover and the ending credits for ) is dope, clever, and fitting for all the seventies nostalgia that Camp Lo conjures up on the album. I love the tribute to , one of the greatest Mafia movies ever.Scout’s Honor…By Way Of Blood (Rampage): Silly, but cleverly unique. One Day It’ll All Make Sense(Common), (The Notorious B.I.G.).

Accept Your Own & Be Yourself (The Black Album) (No I.D.): This award could have gone to any of the candidates (see the Honorable Mentions below), but is a dope album that most of you didn’t even know existed. If the other candidates are sleepers, is comatose. Hatred, Passions And Infidelity.

(Camp Lo): Camp Lo’s luxuriously abstract flows over Ski’s scrumptiously soulful production result in an unheralded classic. (Wu-Tang Clan): Pound for pound, this may be the best hip-hop double album, ever. Yeah, I said it! (Notorious B.I.G.) – Speaking of pounds…the carrier of a .44 Magnum in size 54 drawers boldly and brashly flaunts his polished flow and chiseled wordsmanship over great beats, which unfortunately became his swan song. (Wyclef): A masterful musical adventure orchestrated by the genius Haitian ringmaster.

Cameo Whore: Busta Rhymes (10 cameos) – If you’ve listened to hip-hop any time in the past four decades, this should come as no surprise. I’m willing to bet his name will be called for this award again in the near future. Honorable Mentions: Puffy Daddy (8). Redman (7).
